content: Ultimately, the South African explosives market remains securely anchored by a few highly reliable, compliant, and strategically optimized suppliers capable of supporting the region's intensive mining requirements. The landscape of explosives supply chain risks is shaped by a complex interplay of regulatory changes, logistical challenges, and geopolitical impacts. While historical data specifically detailing South African explosives supply chain disruptions between 2020 and 2023 remains fragmented, recent developments and forward-looking analyses provide critical insights into the vulnerabilities and necessary resilience strategies for the industry as of July 2026. Regulatory changes constitute a primary risk factor that directly impacts explosives supply chain compliance and availability. The regulatory landscape governing explosives in South Africa has undergone significant transformation, reflecting an alignment with both stringent global safety trends and localized industrial priorities. A pivotal development in this domain was the introduction of the 2024 Explosives Regulations, which established comprehensive new compliance measures, rigorous training requirements, and necessary operational adjustments specifically targeted at improving safety standards within the South African mining industry [42] . While the immediate focus of these regulatory amendments centered on occupational health and safety, the broader implications for the supply chain have been profound, requiring suppliers and end-users to adapt to more rigorous compliance protocols that can temporarily affect material availability. Furthermore, the South African Department of Labour has engaged in extensive consultations regarding the amendment of explosives regulations to cultivate what it terms an ideal explosives environment [43] . In tandem with these legislative efforts, the global tightening of explosives management protocols has driven the local adoption of sophisticated compliance technologies. For instance, the industry has increasingly integrated advanced track-and-trace solutions, such as systems developed by Synertech, which are designed to fortify security and ensure strict regulatory compliance across every node of the supply chain [42] .
